parsedVerdict.reasoning: SettleClaim is a standard application use case. The settle method loads the aggregate through the ClaimRepository port, gets coverage terms through the CoverageSource application port, hands the state changes to the domain (claim.decline() and claim.settle(limit, deductible)), saves the result and returns a plain number. The actual settlement math lives in the domain aggregate, not here. The file has no persistence code, no transport or HTTP handling and no framework code. One branch could be read as a business rule: when no coverage terms come back, the claim is declined. But that branch only picks which domain operation to call, which is normal use-case orchestration. Throwing a 'not-found' DomainError when the claim is missing is also ordinary application-level handling. No ADR prose was provided to contradict any of this.
